newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters resume talks in labor dispute.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters resume talks in labor dispute.

text.p: United Parcel Service and Teamsters negotiators resumed talks here on Thursday to try to find a way out of a strike now in its fourth day.

On his way into the talks, Teamsters President Ron Carey emphasised the need for more full-time, rather than part-time, jobs and said he would be looking for signs of flexibility from UPS. "We're making progress, I'll stay to the weekend, whatever is necessary, but if it's just a smokescreen, we're out of here," Carey said.

"What this country needs is good decent fulltime jobs. They don't need jobs that are subcontracted out, they don't need jobs that are part-time. As I've said all straight through, this is about the final needs of working people in America," Carey told reporters outside the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.

Shortly before, UPS Chairman and Chief Executive Officer James Kelly said he welcomed the opportunity to talk, but repeated his call for the Teamsters to put UPS' contract offer to its members for a vote.
"We do have a last, best and final offer on the table," Kelly said. "We are perplexed and don't understand why the Teamsters won't let us send that out to our people," he added.
Teamsters members at UPS have been on strike since Monday, after contract negotiations broke down late on Sunday.
